issue-v17-dist-ops-multigpu-untested.title: High-level distributed ops multi-GPU paths never exercised: 10 'Requires single GPU' skips, yet SyncBatchNorm multi-GPU training calls all_reduce_async

decision-v17-dist-ops-real-multigpu.rationale: Milestone v2.17 targets the last never-run distributed surface: high-level DistributedReduce/AllGather/Broadcast/Barrier multi-GPU paths (10 'Requires single GPU' test skips; the ops header itself defers 'a proper collective test harness'). These ops are NOT dead code - SyncBatchNorm multi-GPU training forward+backward calls DistributedReduce::all_reduce_async at 3 sites. The recoverable bug pattern is identical to R15/R16 (never-run multi-GPU path hides real bugs, e.g. the CPU-coordinated all_reduce reading the caller's device pointer while cudaSetDevice-swapping across all GPUs, and all_reduce_async delegating to a blocking host-staged sync op while ignoring its stream). Plan: (P1) thread-per-rank harness + real multi-GPU tests (proven v2.16 run_per_rank pattern) to expose defects; (P2) converge high-level collectives onto the verified R15/R16 NCCL layer (NcclAllReduce/NcclAllGather/NcclBroadcast/NcclBarrier, current-device routing) or fix legacy paths - decision re-recorded on P1 evidence; (P3) verify SyncBatchNorm multi-GPU gradient path end-to-end. Also tracks R16 review HIGH-B: a rank exiting a collective early poisons the shared NcclContext (readiness/fault exchange hardening in scope).
decision-v17-dist-ops-real-multigpu.alternatives_rejected: Starting on inference/internalization surface instead (recent rounds already covered it); skipping the legacy ops and only documenting the gap (they are live training consumers); re-writing the ops from scratch before gathering test evidence.

DEC-001.rationale: Milestone v2.18: converged DistributedReduce/AllGather/Broadcast onto the verified NCCL layer in v2.17 but deliberately deferred MeshBarrier, the last high-level distributed op still on the legacy per-instance host-event-poll path (barrier.cu, non-threadsafe barriering_ flag, cross-thread cudaEventQuery polling; no real per-rank multi-GPU test — NoDeadlock runs single-host-thread). The R15-R17 pattern is that every never-run multi-GPU surface has hidden real bugs, and MeshBarrier multi-GPU is now effectively never-run (only the single-GPU tests exercise it; the event-poll loop has never been driven from real per-rank threads). Plan: (P1) build a real thread-per-rank multi-GPU MeshBarrier test (synchronize + synchronize_devices driven concurrently per rank) to expose defects and gather evidence; (P2) converge MeshBarrier onto the verified NcclBarrier layer (current_comm routing, sync/async preserved, single-GPU fallback kept) and flip the new tests on; (P3) distributed-ops harness robustness — isolate the tracked harness flake (issue-v17-dist-ops-harness-flake) and the R16 review HIGH-B shared-NcclContext poisoning if a rank exits a collective early (readiness/fault exchange hardening).
DEC-001.alternatives_rejected: Skipping MeshBarrier and closing the milestone (it is the last unconverged v1.1 primitive and its multi-GPU path has never been genuinely exercised); converging barrier.cu wholesale before writing the per-rank test (the P1 evidence-driven flow worked for the three data ops in v2.17); opening a deep-dive milestone instead (the two open issues and the MeshBarrier gap scope this milestone more tightly).
